title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week

    . This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Negative

Friday’s decisive downside reversal extinguished what little buying momentum the market had been building. The major indices have now retreated back below their declining 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, reaffirming the prevailing downtrend and leaving the broader technical picture notably weak.

Market internals have turned firmly negative again, with breadth and momentum indicators deteriorating across the board. Sector and industry leadership is lacking, with defensive areas showing the least weakness rather than true strength, and risk-on areas continuing to lag significantly. Compounding the issue is a near-complete absence of quality technical setups, which makes it increasingly difficult to justify long-side exposure.

Taken together, the weight of evidence offers little incentive for deploying capital aggressively. Until there is a meaningful shift in participation, structure, and internal strength, the market remains a high-risk, low-reward environment for long trades. This is a time to stay defensive, protect capital, and wait patiently for conditions to improve.

Plan of Action

Risk Management and Exposure Control

  • Maintain a Defensive Posture: With major indices below declining 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, the failed breakout attempt reaffirms the need for caution. The short-lived rally attempt highlights the fragility of the market environment.

  • Limit Exposure and Cut Weak Positions: Any long positions that are no longer showing relative strength or holding key support should be reduced or exited. Protecting capital remains the top priority.

  • Avoid Chasing Rallies: The lack of follow-through in the recent upside attempt reinforces the risk of buying into weak bounces. Wait for clear confirmation of strength before increasing exposure.

  • Be Highly Selective with New Trades: If trading at all, focus only on the highest-quality setups — stocks with clean technical patterns, tight consolidations, strong relative strength, and breakout volume.

Market Monitoring and Internal Indicators

  • Breadth and Momentum: Mixed and Fragile

    • Recent selling has eroded internal strength again. While some pockets remain constructive, overall momentum remains tenuous.

  • Monitor Structural Support

    • The integrity of recent higher lows is key. If these levels break, it would suggest the budding uptrend has failed and open the door for deeper downside.

  • Track Sector Performance

    • Strength: Defensive sectors like energy , communication services, and utilities continue to outperform — more due to relative weakness in risk-on areas than true strength.

    • Weakness: Tech, discretionary, and financials remain under pressure, signaling low risk appetite from institutions.

Capital Protection and Tactical Flexibility

  • Maintain Elevated Cash Levels: With volatility high and few compelling opportunities, a defensive cash-heavy position is prudent.

  • Use Tight, Protective Stops: Any active positions should be accompanied by well-defined risk management strategies. Be ready to act swiftly on any signs of renewed selling.

  • Avoid Large Positioning: Keep initial sizes small and only scale up if setups confirm with strength. Avoid broad exposure in a market lacking direction and conviction.

Daily Reassessment and Adaptive Exposure

  • Watch Key Resistance: The 10-, 20-, and 50-day MAs remain significant hurdles. A reclaim and hold above these levels — with volume and confirmation — is necessary before taking on more risk.

  • Adapt Exposure Dynamically:

    • If indices reclaim resistance and internals improve: Gradually scale into high-quality setups.

    • If breakdowns resume: Step back, reduce exposure, and remain in capital preservation mode.

Key Focus Areas

  • Patience and Discipline: The market remains in a vulnerable state. Do not force trades. Let conditions improve before leaning into risk.

  • Monitor for Emerging Leadership: Keep an eye on stocks and sectors forming new bases and showing relative strength. These may be the early movers if a recovery materializes.

  • Stay Flexible and Nimble: Maintain a tactical mindset. Be ready to act — whether that means re-engaging if conditions improve, or retreating quickly if weakness persists.

Bottom Line

The rally attempt has faltered, placing the market back in a vulnerable technical position with no clear leadership or follow-through. Breadth and momentum are mixed, and defensive sectors continue to lead by default. Until the indices can reclaim and hold key moving averages with confirmation from internals, the most prudent course remains caution, capital preservation, and tactical patience.
